# Chronic lymphocytic leukemia

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Hematology and oncology > White blood cell and bone marrow disorders > Chronic lymphocytic leukemia*

[Original Article Link](/library/jT0_q2)

---

## Summary

Chronic <u>lymphocytic</u> <u>leukemia</u> (CLL) is a type of <u>B-cell</u> <u>malignancy</u> that manifests with <u>lymphocytic leukocytosis</u>. CLL is the most common type of <u>leukemia</u> in adults and is typically diagnosed in older individuals (≥ 65 years of age). Clinical features include painless <u>lymphadenopathy</u>, fatigue, chronic <u>pruritus</u>, and increased susceptibility to infections. However, most cases are asymptomatic and diagnosed based on incidental laboratory findings. Diagnosis requires persistent monoclonal <u>B-cell</u> <u>lymphocytosis</u> (â¥ 5000/mmÂ³ for ≥ 3 months) with <u>immunophenotypic</u> markers consistent with CLL on <u>flow cytometry</u>. <u>Peripheral blood smear</u> typically shows a high percentage of small mature <u>lymphocytes</u> and <u>smudge cells</u> (<u>Gumprecht shadows</u>). Several molecular markers are used to predict prognosis and guide treatment, the most important being the negative prognostic markers del(17p) and <u>TP53</u> mutation. Advances in <u>targeted therapy</u> have improved patient outcomes in CLL and <u>small molecule inhibitors</u> (e.g., <u>ibrutinib</u>, <u>venetoclax</u>) are now first-line treatment for most patients. <u>Chemoimmunotherapy</u> may be an effective alternative for some patients. Patients with low-risk disease (<u>Rai stage</u> 0) should be managed expectantly. <u>Allogeneic stem cell transplantation</u> is a curative treatment option but is often not possible because of the older age and multiple comorbidities of most patients with CLL.

---

## Definitions

* Chronic <u>lymphocytic</u> <u>leukemia</u>: a type of proliferative <u>B-cell</u> <u>malignancy</u> that manifests with <u>lymphocytic leukocytosis</u> [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)

* Small lymphocytic lymphoma (<u>SLL</u>): a type of <u>B-cell lymphoma</u> with the same genetic and molecular markers as CLL that manifests primarily in the <u>lymph nodes</u>, <u>bone marrow</u>, and other lymphatic tissue rather than with <u>leukocytosis</u>  [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)[[2]](/library/jXX_B9)





> [!NOTE]
> Some sources classify CLL as a low-grade <u>non-Hodgkin lymphoma</u> because the origin cell is likely a mature <u>B lymphocyte</u>. However, as the malignant cells are present in the blood, it is considered to be a <u>leukemia</u>. <u>SLL</u> is the manifestation of this condition in lymphatic tissue, and is therefore considered to be a <u>lymphoma</u>. [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)

## Epidemiology

* Sex: <u>♂</u> > <u>♀</u> (∼ 2:1)

* Age: The median age at the time of diagnosis is 70–72 years (<u>incidence</u> of CLL increases with age).

* Most common type of <u>leukemia</u> in adults





References:[[3]](/library/vLaAzO)




Epidemiological data refers to the US, unless otherwise specified.

---

## Etiology

### <u>Risk factors</u>




* Older age

* Environmental factors: organic solvents

* <u>Family history</u>

---

## Pathophysiology

<u>Acquired mutations</u> in <u>hematopoietic stem cells</u> → increased <u>proliferation</u> of <u>leukemic</u> <u>B cells</u> with impaired maturation and differentiation in the <u>bone marrow</u>, resulting in:




* Suppression of the <u>proliferation</u> of normal blood cells

* <u>Immunosuppression</u>

* <u>Hypogammaglobulinemia</u>

* <u>Granulocytopenia</u>

* <u>Thrombocytopenia</u>

* <u>Anemia</u>

* Infiltration of the <u>lymph nodes</u>, <u>liver</u>, and <u>spleen</u>

## Clinical features

About half of cases of CLL remain asymptomatic for a long period, resulting in late or incidental diagnosis.




* Weight loss, <u>fever</u>, night sweats, fatigue (<u>B symptoms</u>)

* Painless <u>lymphadenopathy</u>

* <u>Hepatomegaly</u> and/or <u>splenomegaly</u> may occur.

* Repeated infections

* Severe bacterial infections (e.g., <u>necrotic</u> <u>erysipelas</u>)

* Mycosis (<u>candidiasis</u>)

* Viral infections (<u>herpes zoster</u>)

* Symptoms of <u>anemia</u> and <u>thrombocytopenia</u>

* Dermatologic symptoms

* <u>Leukemia cutis</u>

* Chronic <u>pruritus</u>

* <u>Chronic urticaria</u>





> [!TIP]
> <u>Lymphadenopathy</u> is a typical finding in lymphoid malignancies such as CLL and helps to differentiate CLL from <u>CML</u>, a myeloid <u>malignancy</u>.




References:[[3]](/library/vLaAzO)[[4]](/library/peYL-L)

## Diagnosis

### General principles [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)[[2]](/library/jXX_B9)[[5]](/library/FVXgwC)




* Diagnosis requires persistent monoclonal <u>lymphocytosis</u> plus CLL <u>immunophenotype</u> confirmed by <u>flow cytometry</u>.

* Most patients are asymptomatic and evaluated based on incidental laboratory findings.

* <u>Biopsy</u> may be indicated in certain patients, e.g., if the diagnosis is uncertain.

* Refer to <u>hematology</u> or oncology for further evaluation and management.





> [!TIP]
> In patients with confirmed CLL, staging (e.g., using the <u>Rai staging system</u>) and the presence of prognostic markers are used to guide management.




### <u>Laboratory studies</u> [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)[[2]](/library/jXX_B9)[[5]](/library/FVXgwC)[[6]](/library/dVXotC)




Obtain a <u>CBC</u>, <u>peripheral blood smear</u>, and <u>flow cytometry</u> for all patients.




* Diagnostic criteria

* Persistent (≥ 3 months) <u>lymphocytosis</u> (â¥ 5000/mmÂ³)  [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)[[6]](/library/dVXotC)

* CLL <u>immunophenotype</u> confirmed by <u>flow cytometry</u>, including :

* Expression of CD5, <u>CD19</u>, <u>CD20</u> , CD23  [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)

* <u>Light chain restriction</u> (kappa or lambda)

* Additional findings: may further support the diagnosis

* <u>Cytopenias</u> 

* <u>Anemia</u> (usually normochromic, <u>normocytic</u>): may be caused by <u>AIHA</u> [[5]](/library/FVXgwC)[[7]](/library/zN1rdh0)

* <u>Thrombocytopenia</u>

* <u>Granulocytopenia</u>

* <u>Peripheral blood smear</u> may show:

* High percentage of small mature <u>lymphocytes</u>

* <u>Smudge cells</u> (Gumprecht shadows): mature <u>lymphocytes</u> that rupture easily; appear as artifacts on a <u>blood smear</u>  [[8]](/library/NH1-qR0)





> [!TIP]
> The occurrence of both <u>AIHA</u> and <u>ITP</u> is known as <u>Evans syndrome</u>. [[5]](/library/FVXgwC)[[6]](/library/dVXotC)




> [!NOTE]
> In CLL, the <u>smudge cells</u> on a <u>peripheral blood smear</u> look like Crushed Little Lymphocytes.

#### Prognostic markers in CLL [[5]](/library/FVXgwC)




* Indications for testing

* Confirmed CLL diagnosis

* Repeat testing prior to initiating or changing treatment

* Methods  [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)[[5]](/library/FVXgwC)[[6]](/library/dVXotC)

* Cytogenetic testing

* <u>FISH</u> to assess for common <u>structural chromosomal aberrations</u> in CLL, e.g., del(17p)

* <u>Immunoglobulin heavy chain</u> variable region (IGHV) mutational status

* <u>TP53</u> mutational status

* Serum studies: <u>β2-microglobulin</u> and <u>LDH</u>

* Interpretation

* Adverse prognosis: e.g., del(17p) , del(11q), <u>TP53</u> mutation, elevated <u>β2-microglobulin</u>, elevated <u>LDH</u>

* Intermediate prognosis: <u>trisomy</u> 12 [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)

* Favorable prognosis: IGHV mutation , isolated del(13q)





### <u>Biopsies</u> [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)




* <u>Bone marrow aspiration and biopsy</u> [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)

* Not routinely required for diagnosis

* Consider in patients with <u>cytopenias</u> to determine the cause.

* Typical findings in <u>aspirate</u> include a high percentage of small mature <u>lymphocytes</u>.

* <u>Lymph node</u> <u>biopsy</u>: Consider if the diagnosis is uncertain or for the diagnosis of <u>SLL</u> or <u>Richter transformation</u>.

## Classification

### <u>Rai staging system</u>




| <br>Rai staging system [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)[[6]](/library/dVXotC)[[9]](/library/MXXMA9)<br> |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <u>Rai stage</u> | Modified <u>Rai stage</u> | Findings |  |
| 0 | Low risk | Isolated <u>lymphocytosis</u> |  |
| I | Intermediate risk | <u>Lymphocytosis</u> | PLUS <u>lymphadenopathy</u><br> |
| II | PLUS <u>hepatomegaly</u> and/or <u>splenomegaly</u><br> |  |  |
| III | High risk | PLUS <u>anemia</u> (<u>Hb</u> < 11 g/dL) |  |
| IV | PLUS <u>thrombocytopenia</u> (<u>platelets</u> < 100,000/mmÂ³)<br> |  |  |





### Other staging systems [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)




* <u>Binet staging system</u>: commonly used for staging and informing treatment decisions in European countries

* CLL international prognostic index (CLL-IPI): risk <u>stratification</u> score based on age, clinical stage (Rai or Binet), and the presence of prognostic molecular markers





| <br>Binet staging system [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)<br> |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Definition | Additional findings |
| Stage A | <br>* < 3 involved <u>lymph</u> areas<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Hb</u> > 10 g/dL<br><br>* <u>Platelets</u> > 100,000/mmÂ³<br><br><br> |
| Stage B | <br>* ≥ 3 involved <u>lymph</u> areas<br><br> |  |
| <br>Stage C <br> | <br><br>* <u>Anemia</u> (<u>Hb</u> < 10 g/dL)<br><br>* And/or <u>thrombocytopenia</u> (<u>platelets</u> < 100,000/mmÂ³)<br><br><br> |  |

## Treatment

### General principles [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)[[10]](/library/YcXnaC)




Management should be specialist guided. Consider enrollment in a clinical trial.




* Indications for <u>anticancer therapy</u> : based on disease risk (<u>Rai staging</u>) and disease activity [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)

* Low-risk disease (<u>Rai stage</u> 0)

* <u>Expectant management</u>

* Regular follow-ups  to assess for disease progression and indications for treatment [[10]](/library/YcXnaC)

* Intermediate risk disease (<u>Rai stage</u> I or II)

* Consider <u>expectant management</u> if stable and asymptomatic.

* Medical therapy: indicated for progressive or symptomatic disease (i.e., active disease )

* High-risk disease (<u>Rai stage</u> III or IV): medical therapy

* <u>Anticancer therapy</u> may include:

* <u>Targeted therapy</u>, e.g., <u>ibrutinib</u>, <u>rituximab</u>, <u>alemtuzumab</u>

* <u>Chemoimmunotherapy</u>, e.g., FCR: <u>fludarabine</u>, <u>cyclophosphamide</u>, <u>rituximab</u>

* <u>Allogeneic HSCT</u>: currently the only curative treatment option (not routinely performed)





> [!TIP]
> CLL is a <u>malignancy</u> with a slow rate of cell division and disease progression. Treatment of low-risk disease is usually not recommended and is unlikely to extend survival.




### Pretreatment evaluation [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)




* Clinical assessment: <u>physical examination</u>, and <u>functional status assessment</u> (e.g., <u>ECOG</u> score)

* <u>Laboratory studies</u> 

* <u>CMP</u>: to document baseline organ function  [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)[[5]](/library/FVXgwC)

* Repeat cytogenetic testing; see “<u>Prognostic markers in CLL</u>.”

* <u>Immunoglobulin</u> levels: to evaluate for <u>hypogammaglobulinemia</u>  [[5]](/library/FVXgwC)[[6]](/library/dVXotC)

* Infectious disease <u>serology</u>: for <u>HBV</u>, <u>HCV</u>, <u>HIV</u>, and <u>CMV</u>  [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)[[11]](/library/241TiS0)

* <u>Direct Coombs test</u>: to assess for <u>AIHA</u>

* Imaging

* <u>Chest x-ray</u>: to evaluate for <u>mediastinal</u> <u>lymphadenopathy</u>

* Further imaging is not routinely required for diagnosis unless clinically indicated.

* Further testing (e.g., <u>CT scan</u>, <u>bone marrow biopsy</u>): may be necessary for patients enrolling in clinical trials.





![Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score](media/u22dlzv293yvgp9ap3vqnndy.jpg)

Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score




### Pharmacotherapy




* The pretreatment evaluation is used to determine which regimen is used.

* In most patients with CLL, a <u>BTK inhibitor</u> or <u>BCL-2 inhibitor</u> is the first-line treatment.  [[11]](/library/241TiS0)[[12]](/library/pm1Lgh0)[[13]](/library/Jm1sgh0)





| <br>Overview of pharmacotherapy for CLL [[11]](/library/241TiS0)[[14]](/library/261T430)<br> |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Therapy |  | Examples | Indications |
| <u>Targeted therapies</u> | <u>Small molecule inhibitors</u> | <br><br>* <u>BTK inhibitors</u> (e.g., <u>ibrutinib</u>, <u>acalabrutinib</u>)<br><br>* <u>BCL-2 inhibitors</u> (e.g., <u>venetoclax</u>)<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Preferred treatment option for most patients<br><br>* May be used alone or in combination with a <u>monoclonal antibody</u>, e.g., <u>venetoclax</u> PLUS obinutuzumab<br><br><br> |
| <u>Monoclonal antibodies</u> | <br><br>* Anti-<u>CD20</u> <u>antibodies</u>, e.g., <u>rituximab</u>, obinutuzumab, <u>ofatumumab</u><br><br>* Anti-<u>CD52</u> <u>antibodies</u>, e.g., <u>alemtuzumab</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Usually used as an adjunct to a <u>small molecule inhibitor</u> or <u>chemotherapy</u><br><br> |  |
| <u>Chemoimmunotherapy</u> |  | <br><br>* <u>Alkylating agents</u>, e.g., <u>cyclophosphamide</u>, <u>bendamustine</u>, <u>chlorambucil</u><br><br>* <u>Purine analogues</u>, e.g., <u>fludarabine</u>, <u>cladribine</u>, <u>pentostatin</u><br><br>* Recommended regimens, e.g.:<br><br>* <u>Fludarabine</u> PLUS <u>cyclophosphamide</u> PLUS <u>rituximab</u> (FCR): for young patients with few or no comorbidities<br><br>* <u>Bendamustine</u> PLUS <u>rituximab</u> : for older patients and those with low functional status and/or comorbidities<br><br><br> | <br>* May be used in patients without del(17p) or <u>TP53</u> mutation<br><br> |





### <u>Allogeneic stem cell transplantation</u> [[15]](/library/jVX_8C)[[16]](/library/qm1Cgh0)




* Curative treatment for CLL

* High-risk procedure with a 20% <u>mortality rate</u> [[1]](/library/kIYm1q)[[15]](/library/jVX_8C)[[16]](/library/qm1Cgh0)

* Consider for young patients with few or no comorbidities and:

* Del(17p) and/or <u>TP53</u> mutation

* Disease that is refractory to <u>targeted therapy</u>





### <u>Supportive care</u> [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)[[16]](/library/qm1Cgh0)




Evaluate for and manage any complications, including:




* Infectious diseases

* Ensure <u>routine vaccinations</u> (e.g., <u>influenza</u>, <u>pneumococcus</u>) are up-to-date.

* Consider infection prophylaxis (e.g., <u>HHV</u>, <u>VZV</u>, and <u>PCP prophylaxis</u> ). [[16]](/library/qm1Cgh0)

* Consider IVIG therapy for patients with <u>hypogammaglobulinemia</u> who have recurrent infections.

* Autoimmune <u>cytopenias</u>: Manage <u>AIHA</u> and <u>ITP</u> (e.g., with <u>glucocorticoids</u>) as needed.

* <u>Complications of anticancer therapy</u>: Consider the need for <u>G-CSF</u> for <u>anticancer therapy-induced myelosuppression</u>.





> [!WARNING]
> <u>Live vaccines</u> are contraindicated in patients with CLL because of the risk of severe complications. [[2]](/library/jXX_B9)




> [!TIP]
> Infectious diseases are common in patients with CLL. Evaluating for and managing infectious diseases can reduce the risk of severe illness and complications. [[16]](/library/qm1Cgh0)

---

## Complications

* <u>Immunosuppression</u> with subsequent infections (most common <u>cause of death</u>)

* Secondary malignancies

* <u>Hyperviscosity syndrome</u>

* <u>Autoimmune hemolytic anemia</u> (of both the warm and <u>cold agglutinin</u> type)

* Richter transformation or <u>Richter syndrome</u>: transformation into a high-grade <u>NHL</u> (usually diffuse large <u>B cell</u> <u>lymphoma</u>)

* Occurrence: ∼ 5% of cases

* Diagnostic indicators:

* Rapidly progressive <u>lymphadenopathy</u> → <u>lymph node</u> <u>biopsy</u> required

* New onset of <u>B symptoms</u>

* ↑ <u>LDH</u>

* Treatment: similar to symptomatic CLL and advanced stages





References:[[17]](/library/reYfZo)[[18]](/library/7eY4Zo)




We list the most important complications. The selection is not exhaustive.

---

## Prognosis

### Prognostic factors [[6]](/library/dVXotC)




* Older age is associated with a poor overall survival rate.

* <u>Rai staging</u>

* Adverse <u>prognostic markers in CLL</u>, e.g.:

* Del(17p13)

* Elevated <u>β2-microglobulin</u> level

* Blood <u>lymphocyte</u> doubling time: Rapid doubling is associated with a high risk of disease progression.
